skill.summary: Address pull request feedback through guided decisions, validated edits, and approval-gated GitHub responses.

content.value_statement: Pull request feedback can be difficult to track, implement, and answer consistently. This skill guides each decision, validates accepted changes, and previews GitHub responses before posting.
actual_capabilities: Filters automated, resolved, and already answered review comments from the interactive workflow.
Supports one-by-one and batch decision modes for actionable comments.
Applies approved code or documentation changes while preserving unrelated local work.
Runs relevant validation and prepares concise agent-labeled reply drafts.
Previews replies and thread resolutions before performing approved GitHub actions.
limitations: Requires a local checkout of the pull request branch.
Requires authenticated GitHub CLI access to fetch, reply, or resolve threads.
Cannot reliably act when comment identifiers, thread metadata, or repository permissions are unavailable.
Does not post replies, resolve threads, commit, or push without explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Address a Small Review
use_cases.description: Walk through a few review comments, apply selected fixes immediately, and approve each final response.

use_cases.title: Process Large Feedback Batches
use_cases.description: Collect decisions across many comments before applying related changes and validating them together.

use_cases.title: Close Reviewed Threads
use_cases.description: Prepare transparent replies, link pushed fixes when available, and resolve only approved review threads.

prompt_templates.title: Review Comments One by One
prompt_templates.prompt: Walk me through actionable comments on the current pull request one by one. Let me approve each fix before continuing.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants close control over a small review.

prompt_templates.title: Collect Decisions First
prompt_templates.prompt: Review all actionable pull request comments in batch mode. Collect my decision for each comment before editing any files.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants to plan several related changes.

prompt_templates.title: Apply and Validate Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Address accepted review comments, preserve unrelated changes, and run repository-appropriate validation. Prepare concise replies, but do not post them yet.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced contributor needs implementation and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Complete the Review Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Process unresolved review feedback, apply approved changes, offer commit and push, then preview replies and resolutions for final approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer wants an approval-gated workflow through GitHub resolution.

output_examples.input: Explain the comment about missing input validation before I decide.
output_examples.output: The reviewer is concerned that unchecked input can reach the parser. Recommended action: validate the value before parsing, then test invalid input.

output_examples.input: Apply the approved fixes and show me the response preview.
output: Comment 1: reply and resolve. Draft reply explains the added validation and successful focused test.
Comment 2: reply only. Draft reply records the decision to preserve current behavior.
No GitHub actions have been posted.

output_examples.input: Post the approved replies and resolve their threads.
output_examples.output: Posted two agent-labeled replies and resolved one approved thread. One PR-level comment remains open because it has no resolvable thread.

best_practices: Inspect referenced code before recommending a fix when the loaded comment lacks enough context.
Keep every reply concise, specific, and linked to validated work when a pushed commit exists.
Review the final diff and response preview before approving any GitHub action.
anti_patterns: Do not skip uncertain comments merely because they appear automated or previously answered.
Do not combine unrelated refactoring with changes requested by review comments.
Do not post replies, resolve threads, commit, or push before the required approval step.

faq.question: Can this skill only display pull request comments?
faq.answer: No. Use the pr-comments workflow when you only need comments fetched or displayed.

faq.question: Will it change code automatically?
faq.answer: It changes code only after you select or provide a specific response for an actionable comment.

faq.question: Can I review comments in a batch?
faq.answer: Yes. Batch mode collects every decision first, then applies accepted changes together.

faq.question: Will it commit and push changes?
faq.answer: Only when you explicitly approve that step after reviewing validation results and the final diff.

faq.question: How are GitHub replies identified?
faq.answer: Every draft that may be posted begins with the Warp Agent label for clear authorship.

faq.question: What happens when a thread cannot be resolved?
faq.answer: The skill reports the missing metadata or permission and suggests a manual GitHub action instead of guessing.
